sections.title: Warm-up
sections.prompt: Read these three versions aloud. Notice which one gives you energy and which one makes you work.
items: Die Durchführung einer Überprüfung der Unterlagen erfolgt durch die Abteilung.
Der Text ist stilistisch überarbeitet worden.
sections.lede: Style begins in the ear. Hear the difference before you name it.

sections.title: Learning objectives
sections.lede: By the end of this lesson you will be able to revise a text for precision and rhythm.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: Style is not decoration added after the content is finished. It is the sum of choices that decide whether a reader understands, trusts and remembers a text.

blocks.text: At C2 you already control the grammar. The remaining work is editorial: choosing the verb that carries the most meaning, deciding where a sentence should end, and noticing when a nominal construction hides the person doing the action. These choices are not cosmetic. They change how quickly a reader understands and how much authority the text has.
Der Text ist stilistisch überarbeitet worden.
blocks.en: The text has been revised stylistically.

items: A precise verb carries information that an adverb can only approximate: Sie ging langsam becomes Sie schlenderte.
Rhythm is information. A short sentence after a long one lands like a punch line; three long sentences in a row blur together.
Nominalisation raises the register but lowers the energy. Turn nouns back into verbs when the agent matters.
Redundancy is not emphasis. Bereits schon and weißer Schimmel repeat rather than reinforce.
Register is consistency, not formality. One colloquial word can break an otherwise formal paragraph.

blocks.title: The read-aloud test
blocks.text: Read the paragraph aloud at a normal pace. Where you run out of breath, the reader will lose the thread. Where you stumble, the syntax is probably doing too much.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: Most stylistic revision happens in four moves: sharpen the verb, cut the frame, split the sentence, restore the agent.

rows: fixed collocation; machen is too general
one precise verb replaces verb plus adverb
Es ist wichtig zu beachten, dass …
Der Betrieb verfügt über eine Kantine.
the plain verb is stronger here

items: Keep one main idea per sentence. If a sentence needs two commas and a parenthesis, it probably needs two sentences.
Vary length deliberately: a long sentence can build context, but the next one should release it.
Funktionsverbgefüge such as zur Verfügung stellen are not errors. They are useful in administration, but they are usually longer and weaker than the verb they hide.
Cut adjectives that repeat the noun: ein großer Riese, ein kleiner Zwerg, eine totale Vollendung.
Prefer the active voice when responsibility matters. The passive is honest when the agent is unknown or irrelevant, and evasive when it is not.

sections.title: Vocabulary
sections.lede: The vocabulary of revision is itself precise. Learn the words you need to explain a change.

items.example: Ein prägnanter Satz bleibt im Gedächtnis.
items.exampleEn: A concise sentence stays in the memory.

items.example: Anschauliche Beispiele machen das Argument überzeugend.
items.exampleEn: Vivid examples make the argument convincing.

items.example: Diese Wendung wirkt in einem Bericht zu umgangssprachlich.
items.exampleEn: This phrase sounds too colloquial in a report.

items.example: Nach der Überarbeitung ist der Text deutlich kürzer.
items.exampleEn: After the revision the text is considerably shorter.

items.example: Zu viel Nominalstil macht den Text schwer verständlich.
items.exampleEn: Too much nominal style makes the text hard to understand.

items.example: Die Straffung des Absatzes hat den Inhalt geschärft.
items.exampleEn: Tightening the paragraph sharpened the content.

sections.title: Example sentences
sections.lede: Each pair shows a choice, not a correction. Ask what the second version gains and what it loses.

items.de: Der Text ist stilistisch überarbeitet worden.
items.en: The text has been revised stylistically.
items.note: The passive keeps the focus on the text; the reviser is irrelevant here.

items.de: Statt „eine Entscheidung machen“ sagt man treffender „eine Entscheidung treffen“.
items.en: Instead of “eine Entscheidung machen”, the more apt phrase is “eine Entscheidung treffen”.
items.note: Treffen is the conventional collocation; machen is grammatical but vague.

items.de: Der Autor hätte den Satz straffen können, ohne Inhalt zu verlieren.
items.en: The author could have tightened the sentence without losing content.
items.note: A counterfactual judgement about style, not about facts.

items.de: Kurze Sätze wirken nach einem langen Satz wie ein Atemzug.
items.en: After a long sentence, short sentences feel like a breath.
items.note: The image explains rhythm better than an abstract rule.

items.de: Anschaulich schreiben heißt: zeigen, nicht behaupten.
items.en: Writing vividly means showing, not asserting.
items.note: The colon prepares a definition and gives the sentence a clean ending.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: These words are common in editorial discussion. Stress them correctly and you will sound as if you belong in the conversation.

items.hint: Stress the second syllable: prä-GNANT. The g is voiced and the final t is crisp.
Start with a clear “an”, then the au diphthong, then a soft ch: AN-schau-lich.
Short e, clear final -ung. Do not turn the final g into a hard English g.
Stress the final syllable: re-dun-DANZ. The z is pronounced “ts”.
Stress the first syllable; th is simply t: RÜT-mus.

sections.title: Cultural note
sections.heading: Why German style guides attack the noun

blocks.text: German has a long tradition of style advice that treats clarity as a civic virtue. Wolf Schneider's journalism handbooks, widely used in German newsrooms and journalism schools, argue for short sentences, strong verbs and a visible agent. The target is often called Amtsdeutsch or Behördensprache: the nominal, passive style associated with official letters.

This does not make nominalisation wrong. Academic and legal German needs it, because it allows precise reference to abstract entities. The stylistic question is always purpose: a contract may need die Inanspruchnahme einer Leistung, while a newspaper report is usually better served by the verb.

sections.title: Dialogue in context
sections.lede: An editor and an author revise one paragraph. Listen for the moment the author accepts the change.
sections.setting: Editing session between a publisher and an author

lines.speaker: Lektorin
lines.de: Der Absatz ist inhaltlich stark, aber er trägt zu viele Nominalisierungen.
lines.en: The paragraph is strong in content, but it carries too many nominalisations.

lines.speaker: Autor
lines.de: Sie meinen die Wendungen wie „zur Durchführung gelangen“?
lines.en: You mean the phrases like “zur Durchführung gelangen”?

lines.speaker: Lektorin
lines.de: Genau. „Wir führen die Prüfung durch“ ist kürzer und lebendiger.
lines.en: Exactly. “Wir führen die Prüfung durch” is shorter and more alive.

lines.speaker: Autor
lines.de: Und der lange Satz am Anfang?
lines.en: And the long sentence at the beginning?

lines.speaker: Lektorin
lines.de: Den würde ich teilen. Ein kurzer Satz danach setzt den Akzent.
lines.en: I would split that one. A short sentence after it sets the accent.

lines.speaker: Autor
lines.de: Einverstanden. Ich überarbeite die Passage bis morgen.
lines.en: Agreed. I'll revise the passage by tomorrow.

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: Vom Nominalstil zum Verbalstil
sections.lede: The same content can be packaged as a noun or as a verb. The choice controls pace and responsibility.

rows: the action and its object become visible

items: Nominalisation is useful when the action itself is the topic: Die Prüfung der Daten dauert zwei Tage.
Turn a noun back into a verb when you want to name the agent: Wir prüfen die Daten.
Funktionsverbgefüge are not automatically bad, but check whether the verb they hide would be shorter and clearer.
A sentence beginning with Es ist wichtig, dass … often loses nothing when the frame is removed.
When you split a sentence, give the second half a job: a consequence, a contrast or an example.

sections.tip: Edit in two passes. First cut what is redundant, then vary sentence length. Trying to do both at once makes you cautious, and cautious editing produces flat prose.

sections.title: Choose the right answer
sections.lede: Choose the version a careful editor would prefer — and be ready to say why.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is the most concise?
options: Die Kommission kam zu einer Entscheidung.
Die Kommission hat eine Entscheidung getroffen.
exercises.explanation: Die Kommission entschied replaces a light verb plus noun with one precise verb. The other versions are grammatical but longer.

exercises.prompt: Which verb collocates naturally with Entscheidung?
exercises.explanation: The standard collocation is eine Entscheidung treffen. Eine Entscheidung machen is a common learner error.

options: Der weiße Schimmel stand auf der Wiese.
Der Schimmel stand auf der Wiese.
Das Pferd stand auf der Wiese.
Ein Tier stand auf der Wiese.
exercises.explanation: A Schimmel is by definition a white horse, so weißer Schimmel repeats the same information.

exercises.prompt: Which revision turns nominal style into verbal style?
options: Die Durchführung der Prüfung erfolgt am Montag. → Die Prüfung wird am Montag durchgeführt.
Die Prüfung findet am Montag statt. → Die Prüfung wird am Montag stattfinden.
Die Prüfung ist am Montag. → Am Montag ist die Prüfung.
Die Prüfung dauert lange. → Die Durchführung der Prüfung dauert lange.
exercises.explanation: The noun Durchführung becomes the verb durchgeführt. The other options keep the structure or add nominal weight.

exercises.prompt: What is the usual effect of a short sentence after a long one?
options: It creates emphasis and gives the reader a pause.
It makes the text more formal.
It removes the need for paragraphs.
exercises.explanation: The contrast in length creates emphasis. The short sentence lands because the long one has built up momentum.

exercises.prompt: Which verb most precisely describes walking slowly and without purpose?
exercises.explanation: Schlendern means to stroll or saunter. Gehen is neutral, laufen is faster, and marschieren suggests purpose and discipline.

sections.title: Complete the sentence
sections.lede: Type the missing word. In several items the answer is the precise verb, not the noun.

exercises.explanation: The collocation is eine Entscheidung treffen: die Kommission trifft eine Entscheidung.
Überarbeiten means to revise or rework; the participle is überarbeitet.

exercises.prompt: Zu viel ___ macht den Text schwer verständlich.
exercises.explanation: Der Nominalstil is the noun-heavy style that slows a text down.

exercises.prompt: Die Autorin ___ die Handlung auf das Wesentliche.
exercises.explanation: Straffen means to tighten or streamline: sie strafft die Handlung.

exercises.prompt: Nach der ___ ist der Text deutlich kürzer.
exercises.explanation: Die Überarbeitung is the revision; nach der Überarbeitung = after the revision.

exercises.prompt: Statt „zur Anwendung kommen“ sagt man kürzer „___ werden“.
exercises.explanation: The verbal alternative is angewendet werden, a direct passive instead of the nominal phrase.

sections.title: Build the sentence
sections.lede: Build clean sentences. Each one models a revision principle from this lesson.

exercises.prompt: Build: “The text has been revised stylistically.”
exercises.answer: Der Text ist stilistisch überarbeitet worden.
exercises.explanation: The passive with sein + participle + worden keeps the focus on the text.
Kurze is an adjective before the noun; the verb schaffen takes the accusative object Klarheit.

exercises.prompt: Build: “A decision is only made after review.”
exercises.answer: Eine Entscheidung wird erst nach Prüfung getroffen.
exercises.explanation: The passive frame wird … getroffen surrounds the adverbial phrase erst nach Prüfung.

exercises.prompt: Build: “Vivid examples make the argument convincing.”
exercises.answer: Anschauliche Beispiele machen das Argument überzeugend.
exercises.explanation: Machen takes two accusative objects here: das Argument and the predicate adjective überzeugend.

sections.title: Listening
sections.lede: An editor describes her revision process. Listen once for the problem, once for the method.
sections.speaker: An editor talking about her work

script.speaker: Lektorin
script.de: Ich habe den Absatz dreimal gelesen. Beim ersten Mal war er korrekt, beim zweiten langweilig und beim dritten endlich klar.
script.en: I read the paragraph three times. The first time it was correct, the second time boring, and the third time finally clear.

script.speaker: Lektorin
script.de: Das Problem waren nicht die Fakten, sondern die vielen Nominalisierungen.
script.en: The problem was not the facts, but the many nominalisations.

script.speaker: Lektorin
script.de: Aus „zur Durchführung gelangen“ wurde „durchführen“, aus einem Satz mit vierundvierzig Wörtern zwei Sätze mit je zwanzig.
script.en: “Zur Durchführung gelangen” became “durchführen”, and one sentence of forty-four words became two sentences of twenty each.

script.speaker: Lektorin
script.de: Der Inhalt ist derselbe geblieben, aber der Leser findet ihn jetzt.
script.en: The content has stayed the same, but now the reader can find it.

questions.prompt: What was the main problem with the paragraph?
questions.explanation: She says the problem was not the facts but the many nominalisations.

questions.prompt: What happened to the long sentence?
options: It was divided into two sentences.
It was moved to the end.
questions.explanation: One sentence of forty-four words became two sentences of twenty each.

questions.prompt: What is the result of the revision?
options: The content is the same but easier to find.
questions.explanation: Der Inhalt ist derselbe geblieben, aber der Leser findet ihn jetzt — the content is unchanged and more accessible.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Revise a sentence out loud, then justify the change in one clear sentence.
sections.prompt: Revise this sentence aloud and explain your choice: „Die Durchführung einer Überprüfung der Unterlagen erfolgt durch die Abteilung.“

model.de: Die Abteilung prüft die Unterlagen. Der Satz ist kürzer, nennt den Handelnden und verliert keine Information. Das Verb trägt jetzt die Handlung, statt sie in einem Substantiv zu verstecken.
model.en: The department checks the documents. The sentence is shorter, names the agent and loses no information. The verb now carries the action instead of hiding it in a noun.

tips: Name the agent first. If the sentence does not tell you who acts, the passive may be hiding responsibility.
Replace one nominal phrase at a time, then read the result aloud. Revision is iterative, not a single rewrite.
Justify your change with a criterion: shorter, clearer, more precise or better rhythm. Vague praise is not stylistic analysis.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: These are not grammar errors. They are choices that make a text sound less controlled.

items.why: German nouns have preferred verb partners. Treffen is the standard collocation; machen is grammatical but vague.

items.wrong: Der Text wurde einer Überarbeitung unterzogen, wodurch eine Verbesserung erzielt werden konnte.
items.right: Der Text wurde überarbeitet und dadurch besser.
items.why: The first version stacks three nominalisations around one simple action. The revision says the same thing in half the words.

items.wrong: Das Projekt ist bereits schon abgeschlossen.
items.why: Bereits and schon mean the same thing. Using both is redundancy, not emphasis.

items.wrong: Der Betrieb verfügt über eine eigene Kantine.
items.right: Der Betrieb hat eine eigene Kantine.
items.why: Verfügen über is not wrong, but in a plain report hat is shorter and less bureaucratic. Choose the register deliberately.

questions.explanation: Schlendern means to stroll. The other verbs are neutral or faster.

questions.prompt: Which version is the strongest verbal revision?
options: Die Durchführung der Prüfung erfolgt am Montag.
Die Prüfung wird am Montag durchgeführt.
Die Prüfung findet am Montag ihre Durchführung.
Am Montag kommt die Prüfung zur Durchführung.
questions.explanation: The direct passive with durchgeführt is shorter and clearer than the nominal phrases around Durchführung.
Die Kommission trifft eine Entscheidung — the fixed collocation uses treffen.
The participle of überarbeiten is überarbeitet.

questions.prompt: Zu viel ___ macht den Text schwer verständlich.
questions.explanation: Der Nominalstil is the noun-heavy style that reduces readability.

questions.prompt: Build: “The text has been revised stylistically.”
questions.answer: Der Text ist stilistisch überarbeitet worden.
questions.explanation: The passive is sein + past participle + worden; the adverb stilistisch stands before the participle.
Kurze agrees with the plural noun Sätze; schaffen takes the accusative object Klarheit.
